title: Classification of extremity movements by visual observation of signals and their transforms
author: Hernandez, Ziegelman, et al.

steps.title: Generate movement signals for participants
steps.instruction: Collect raw movement data for each participant performing the five repetitive tasks (finger tapping, hand movements, pronation‑supination, toe tapping, leg agility) as described in sections 3.4‑3.8, then store the time‑series signals for each extremity (finger, wrist, ankle, toe).

steps.title: Create signal and transform images
steps.instruction: For each stored signal, produce separate image panels: (a) the original time‑domain signal together with its Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) (reference [12]), and (b) the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) without the original signal (reference [13]). Arrange the x‑, y‑, and z‑axis plots side‑by‑side for each extremity; for finger‑wrist pairs place finger plots in the upper row and wrist plots in the lower row (Fig 1), for ankle‑toe pairs place ankle plots upper and toe plots lower (Fig 2). For averaged two‑session data, generate a single panel showing the average x, y, z axes for each extremity (Fig 3, Fig 4).

steps.title: Randomize image order and blind identifiers
steps.instruction: Randomly shuffle all image panels so that raters cannot infer laterality (left/right) or clinical status (PD, MSA, TD). For single‑assessment cohorts (MSA, PD) present six‑image panels per participant; for the two‑assessment PD/TD cohort present two averaged panels per participant. Ensure four random orders for the MSA man (two signal + FFT, two CWT) as described.

steps.title: Prepare rating sheets
steps.instruction: Below each image panel provide a space for raters to mark the presence or absence of each predefined abnormality (as in reference [11]). Use identical sheets for all sessions.

steps.title: Conduct MSA single‑session rating
steps.instruction: Present the six‑image panels of the single MSA participant to each rater. Require the rater to complete all six ratings before moving to any other project.

steps.title: Conduct PD single‑session rating
steps.instruction: Present the six‑image panels of each of the ten PD participants (single assessment) to the raters. Require completion of 40 FFT representations and 40 CWT representations (10 participants × 4 extremities) before proceeding.

steps.title: Conduct PD/TD two‑session rating
steps.instruction: Present the two averaged panels (finger‑wrist or ankle‑toe) for each of the 20 PD participants and the eight TD participants. Raters must finish all 148 CWT representations in a counter‑balanced pseudorandomized order that balances motor‑impairment difficulty across presentations.

steps.title: Enforce sequential session order
steps.instruction: Raters must complete the MSA session first, then the PD single‑session, and finally the PD/TD two‑session groups, without skipping ahead.

steps.title: Apply signal processing algorithms
steps.instruction: Run the custom signal‑processing scripts (references [14, 16]) on the raw data to extract the five repetitive movement outputs. Compute FFTs (reference [15]) and CWTs (reference [17]) for each extremity.

steps.title: Document environmental conditions
steps.instruction: Perform all rating sessions with participants seated in straight‑back chairs with armrests and no wheels. Note that chairs may differ between rooms and ambient temperature may vary; record the room temperature if relevant.

description: The method was applied to the cohorts of participants with PD, MSA, and TD. Signal processing algorithms [14,16] were written to extract and analyze the data. FFTs [15] and CWTs [17] were applied to the output of the five repetitive movements of all participants. Single test analysis was applied to the signals of one man with MSA and ten participants with PD. Test sessions with a repeat test session a month or so later was performed on 20 participants with Parkinson's disease and eight healthy control participants with TD [9]. These data are being analyzed for future publications. Raters were given representations as six images of the output of each extremity of the man with MSA as test and retest expressions [9,11]. They were randomly presented to all raters in four random orders, resulting in the evaluation of two signal and FFT representations and two CWT without signal representations [9]. Raters were required to complete the ratings of the man with MSA before proceeding to the next project. Raters were then asked to complete ratings of representations as six images of the output of each extremity of ten participants with PD who completed single rating sessions [9,11]. Raters were required to complete the ratings of 40 FFT representations and 40 CWT representations from the ten participants with PD who completed single ratings before proceeding to the next project [9]. Raters were then asked to complete ratings of representations as two images of the output of each extremity of 20 participants with PD and eight age- and sex-matched healthy participants with TD who completed two rating sessions [9]. Overall, raters were required to complete the ratings of 148 CWT representations in a counterbalanced pseudorandomized design that controlled for the difficulty of the ratings by balancing the level of motor impairment across presentations [9].
